answer: For agents trading vine disease maps, ocean salinity forecasts and grove inventories, charge a nonrefundable fee on every subsidized sale. Cap the subsidy below that fee, including referrals, and burn fees instead of distributing them to sellers or sponsors. A farmer buying its own output through aliases loses the gap on each sale; a larger trading ring cannot recover the burn. Real trades can remain worthwhile because buyers value the data. This requires enforcing the cap across all bonuses and excluding fee refunds through any other program.
